items.evidence: oshb:Song.5.9 (byte tier) is entirely one turn by the daughters (2fs address suffix on 'your beloved,' asking the taunt-question) with no reply inside the row; the answer is split into a separate row (wasf_poem, web:Song.5.10-Song.5.16). The strategy defines dialogue_exchange as 'rapid attributed alternation held as ONE unit' and names its own expected zone as '5:9 + 6:1 daughters-questions WITH THEIR ANSWERS' -- this row realizes neither the alternation nor the pairing. A single-voice turn bounded by tier-1 voice shifts on both edges (the 5:8 refrain close before it; the voice/genre shift into her wasf at 5:10 after it) is the closed vocabulary's lyric_address pattern, and device_notes discloses only the intra-verse quote-doubling, not a one-sentence deviation justification for choosing dialogue_exchange over that default.

items.claim: The row denies any marker separating 6:5-7 from 6:8-9, but the bytes show a real grammatical-person shift at that join (2fs address suffix giving way to pure third-person report), which the strongest_rejected_alternative never engages in its byte-grounded form.
items.evidence: oshb:Song.6.7 (byte tier) closes on a 2fs-suffixed noun in direct address ('your temple'); oshb:Song.6.8-Song.6.9 (byte tier) carry zero second-person suffixes -- a complete shift to third-person description ('she is one,' 'her mother,' 'the daughters... praised her'), re-verified against verse_map_oshb.json. The owner's moderate VOICE-ATTRIBUTION policy names in-verse gendered suffix/verb-form shifts as tier-1 evidence, so the row's blanket 'no tier-1 voice-shift marker separates' claim overstates the case. The rejected_alternative frames the rival only as a 'genre' split (body-part imagery vs. numeric comparison), never as this stronger, byte-grounded person-shift rival. The row's ultimate call (hold together, same male speaker) may still be right on an enallage reading -- the strategy itself allows person-shift-without-speaker-shift at 1:2-4 -- but that argument is never made; the marker is denied rather than engaged and distinguished from a genuine speaker change.
tier_citations: tier-1 (uncited by row): 2fs suffix in oshb:Song.6.7 (byte) vs. third-person forms in oshb:Song.6.8-Song.6.9 (byte)

items.claim: The claim that 6:10 is 'bounded on both sides by a person-form shift' holds only on the back edge (6:10 into 6:11); the front edge (6:9 into 6:10) shows no person-form shift -- both verses are third-person feminine singular about the same referent.
items.evidence: oshb:Song.6.9's closing clauses (byte tier) are uniformly third-person ('she,' 'her mother,' 'the daughters saw her'), and oshb:Song.6.10 (byte tier) opens with a third-person feminine question ('who is this') continuing reference to the same 'she' -- re-verified against verse_map_oshb.json, there is no morphological person shift between them, contrary to the row's characterization of 6:9 as a 'mixed address-and-report voice' distinct from 6:10's third person. The genuine shift the row also cites (third person to first-person singular at the open of oshb:Song.6.11, byte tier) is real and correctly grounds the back boundary alone. The front boundary needs a different byte warrant -- e.g. the declarative-to-question form change, or the mi-zot formula anchor itself -- not the bilateral person-shift claim as stated.
tier_citations: tier-1 (claim tested): third-person forms in oshb:Song.6.9 and oshb:Song.6.10 (byte) vs. first-person singular verb opening oshb:Song.6.11 (byte)

items.evidence: oshb:Song.6.12 (byte tier) closes in first-person singular; oshb:Song.7.1 (= web:Song.6.13, byte tier) opens with a repeated 2fs imperative summons addressed to 'the Shulammite' -- an epithet that does not recur elsewhere in the book's device inventory -- a clear person/addressee shift, re-verified against verse_map_oshb.json.
